PullRequest.Title: eslint: fix bracket notation in build scripts
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

- replace bracket notation with dot notation for identifier-like properties in the Build, CI, and scripts cleanup group
- remove all 48 cleaned paths in that group from `.eslint-allowed-bracket-notation-files`

This PR is intentionally stacked on #334756, which enables `local/code-no-bracket-notation-for-identifiers`. Its base should be changed to `main` after #334756 merges.

## Validation

- targeted ESLint with `--max-warnings=0` across all 48 cleaned files
- `npm run typecheck` from `build`
- targeted hygiene across all 49 changed files
- `git diff --check`

Scenarios.Scenario: Developer dependency installation and prelaunch preparation
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The install-state check gates npm/node-gyp subprocesses; prelaunch checks node_modules, Electron version, and compiled output before potentially running npm ci, Electron download, or compilation. These operations remain on the same critical path as before.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read install state, .nvmrc, npm configuration, Electron version, and dependency directories.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: A bounded set of startup checks plus existing scans determined by configured install directories.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same environment properties controlled identical filesystem checks and fast paths through bracket notation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Checks determine whether expensive install/download/compile work can be skipped.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run npm installs, node-gyp preparation, git configuration, Electron download, and compilation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Native install tasks remain sequential; JavaScript-only directory installs remain capped at min(CPU count, 8); prelaunch subprocesses run only on cache misses.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical subprocesses, gating, and concurrency were selected from the same environment values via bracket notation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These subprocesses block completion of installation or prelaunch when their existing cache gates miss.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Configured dependency directories and whether install/Electron/output caches are warm; effective parallel npm install cardinality remains capped at eight.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Native build/remote installs are sequential and JavaScript-only installs use the unchanged eight-worker maximum; prelaunch steps remain sequential.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Install-state and Electron-version fast paths are unchanged; force flags still bypass the same caches, and no cache keys or negative-cache behavior changed.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: dot and bracket access use the same literal property keys on the same environment objects, and surrounding control flow is unchanged.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual install duration varies by machine and network, but the diff does not alter whether or how often any expensive operation runs.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression: property-access syntax changes do not alter critical-path work, cache outcomes, or concurrency.

Scenarios.Scenario: CI build publication, signing, packaging, and artifact upload
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Credential construction and environment-controlled branch selection precede existing Cosmos/Azure requests, signing processes, archive creation, and uploads; the diff leaves all awaits and process creation unchanged.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Execute the createBuild Cosmos stored procedure and upload web artifacts to Azure storage.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One retried createBuild procedure per invocation; CDN uploads remain one per artifact plus one files.txt upload.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same credentials, endpoint, commit, and quality values fed the same network calls through bracket notation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Pipeline completion waits for the database operation and upload streams.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run ESRP signing, PowerShell packaging, 7-Zip archive/list operations, and setup signing.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Three signing tasks are still started in parallel for non-exploration builds, followed by at most three archive pairs and one setup-signing task based on existing build flags.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same quality and build flags selected the same process set and ordering through bracket notation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Signing and packaging block artifact production.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Build signing metadata/JWS headers and upload file listings.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One signing header per request and one listing proportional to uploaded artifact count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same properties were assigned with bracket notation; byte volume and allocation cardinality are unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Serialization occurs before the corresponding signing request or final listing upload.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number and size of build artifacts and signing file groups; no grouping or effective cardinality changed.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing parallel signing and split compressed/uncompressed upload streams are unchanged; no new burst or limiter change was introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Immutable CDN cache-control and existing retry behavior remain unchanged; the diff changes no cache key, hit path, or retry policy.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: every changed expression resolves the same identifier-like property and no call, await, stream, loop, or condition was added.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Pipeline cost depends on artifact size and external service latency, but these inputs and boundary counts are identical before and after.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression: expensive boundary count, scheduling, serialization size, and critical-path placement are unchanged.

Scenarios.Scenario: OSS license scanning and notice merging
Scenarios.CriticalPath: CLI argument parsing selects repository/input/output paths, after which the existing recursive scans, optional network resolution, parsing, sorting, and synchronous output writes run.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Recursively discover manifests, read package and notice files, and write notice/presence/stub/unresolved outputs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Reads and writes continue to scale with shipped extensions/packages and the same fixed set of output indexes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same parsed argument values selected the same files via bracket notation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Scanning, merging, and writes block command completion.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch license data for components not already covered by Component Governance.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Effective calls remain limited to unresolved, deduplicated components after the unchanged CG coverage set is loaded.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same optional CG path and coverage gate were read from the same args object through bracket notation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required resolution calls remain on the scan critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of extensions, package manifests, Cargo locks, and unresolved deduplicated components.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No loop, queue, Promise aggregation, limiter, or request scheduling changed.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The existing Component Governance coverage set suppresses redundant fetches exactly as before; sibling presence/stub/unresolved indexes use the same paths.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: all changed accesses are literal-key syntax substitutions on the same parsed args object.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Repository/package cardinality can be large, but no changed line increases it or repeats work.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression: scan cardinality, deduplication, filesystem traffic, and optional network fan-out are unchanged.

Scenarios.Scenario: Local web and sessions development server startup and requests
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Startup parses arguments, optionally downloads playground extensions or scans CSS files, then starts the server; sessions root requests serialize an import map and static requests perform file metadata/read operations.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Glob or recursively scan compiled CSS at startup and stat/stream static files per request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One startup scan proportional to CSS files; up to two metadata checks and one stream per static request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same host, port, and mock values were obtained through bracket notation, with identical scanning and request handling.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: CSS discovery precedes listen; static reads serve each request.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Download playground extension files when explicitly requested.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Only the existing fixed extension file set on the playground cache-miss path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same playground and verbose flags selected the same download path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Downloads must finish before playground server startup.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Spawn @vscode/test-web and optionally open a browser.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One server subprocess and at most one browser launch per invocation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same parsed argument values controlled identical subprocesses.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Server process startup is required for the workflow; browser launch is subsequent user-facing startup work.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Generate and stringify the CSS import map for a sessions root-page response.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One O(number of CSS modules) serialization per root/index request, as before.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Only access to the mock flag changed syntax; CSS module cardinality and serialization frequency are unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: HTML response completion waits for serialization.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of compiled CSS modules and HTTP requests; playground download count remains the existing fixed asset set.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Node HTTP handling and child-process behavior are unchanged; no queue, limiter, or fan-out was modified.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing playground directory checks and compiled-output reuse remain unchanged; no cache key or invalidation behavior changed.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: changed argument reads are semantically identical and do not move work into request handlers or add requests.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Large CSS output can make root-page generation noticeable, but that behavior is pre-existing and not amplified by this diff.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression: startup boundaries, per-request serialization, and process/network cardinality are unchanged.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all 49 changed files and every patch page for the performance focus. The PR exclusively replaces bracket notation with dot notation for identifier-like properties and removes the corresponding lint allowlist entries. Traced representative install/prelaunch, CI publication/signing, license scan/merge, and local web-server scenarios; no changed line adds work, changes cache behavior, increases boundary cardinality, alters concurrency, or retains additional state. No performance findings and no regression-fix learning record.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
